crusadecraft.lieu.title: Places
crusadecraft.lieu.open.tip: Every place in the world, nested under one another, with their sheets.
crusadecraft.lieu.sheet.tip: This place's sheet, in the places screen.
crusadecraft.lieu.origin.detached: gone from the world: only its sheet remains
crusadecraft.lieu.new.tip: A title (empire, kingdom, duchy…) that groups other places, or a place: holy site, ruin, region. It goes under the chosen place.
crusadecraft.lieu.new.survival.tip: A holy site, a ruin or a region, on your lands. Easiest: the boundary staff in Place mode.
crusadecraft.lieu.write.tip: Write this place's sheet: its history, what is found there. The mod writes nothing in it.
crusadecraft.lieu.write.title: Place sheet
crusadecraft.lieu.write.hint: What you want to say about this place…
crusadecraft.lieu.reparent.tip: File this place under another (a duchy under a kingdom, a town under a county…).
crusadecraft.lieu.holder.tip: The realm that holds this place.
crusadecraft.lieu.delete.tip: Deletes this place and its sheet. What was under it falls back to the place the world gives it.
crusadecraft.lieu.none_yet: The world has no places yet: found a realm, generate the computer realms, or place one.
crusadecraft.lieu.pick: Pick a place in the list to see its sheet.
crusadecraft.lieu.text.empty: This place has no sheet yet.
crusadecraft.lieu.text.empty.writer: This place has no sheet yet. The Write button lets you write it.
crusadecraft.lieu.form.title_hint: Only the place name: Normandy gives Duchy of Normandy
crusadecraft.lieu.form.name_hint: The full name: Abbey of Saint-Aubin
crusadecraft.lieu.form.kind.title.tip: A title groups other places; it has no position.
crusadecraft.lieu.form.kind.place.tip: A place is set where you stand (or where the staff aimed).
crusadecraft.lieu.form.under.tip: Click to file it under the place chosen in the screen, or under none.
crusadecraft.lieu.form.holder.help: Click to cycle through the realms.
crusadecraft.lieu.form.parent.world.tip: The place takes back the parent the world gives it: a realm's liege, the realm holding a town.
crusadecraft.lieu.form.parent.help: Click the place it will come under.
crusadecraft.lieu.kind_refused: This kind of place comes from something else: a town is set on the map, a construction with the staff.
crusadecraft.lieu.bad_name: A name is needed, %s letters at most.
crusadecraft.lieu.no_realm: You need a realm to place one.
crusadecraft.lieu.not_your_land: This is not on your lands.
crusadecraft.lieu.too_many: Too many places set by hand (%s at most).
crusadecraft.lieu.rename_elsewhere: This place is renamed where it was born: the map for a town or a realm, the Town Hall for a colony.
crusadecraft.lieu.cycle: Impossible: a place cannot come under one of its own.
crusadecraft.lieu.holder_elsewhere: This place's holder comes from the world: it changes through war or on the map.
crusadecraft.lieu.delete_elsewhere: This place will go with what it was born from (the town, the construction, the realm).
crusadecraft.bornage.mode.lieu.tip: Right-click the ground: a holy site, a ruin or a region, which you then name.
crusadecraft.bornage.help.lieu: Right-click the ground: you name the place, then it is set there.
crusadecraft.bornage.lieu.tip: Place: %s. You name it right after the click.
crusadecraft.codex.lieux.p0: The $(l)Places$() screen (Places button in the royal menu or on the map) files the whole world: realms under their lieges, towns under their realms, forts under their towns. Each place has its $(l)sheet$(): who holds it, what it comes under, its population, and the text you write in it.
crusadecraft.codex.lieux.p1: The host can set titles that group other places (Duchy of Normandy) and file each place wherever they like. In survival, you set on your lands a $(l)holy site$(), a $(l)ruin$() or a $(l)region$(): boundary staff in Place mode, a click on the ground, a name.
